Official links: cleanyour.tv and this repo. Other domains using the name, such as cleanyourtv.com, are not run by this project ( #1004 ). CleanYourTV publishes no app in any app store, and clean-your-tv.net is not ours either.
How it works · Quick start · What you get · Supported TVs · Doing it by hand · The launcher · Restoring · Firmware updates · Questions · Contributing
Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling:
No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.
The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask before touching anything you might use.
The three steps below are written for a coding assistant: the computer needs to be on the same Wi-Fi as the TV, with a shell on it, plus Python 3, a JDK from 17 through 22, and Android SDK platform 34 with build-tools 34 (the assistant builds the launcher there). Without an assistant, Doing it by hand is the same job, run by you, and it has the install commands.
Any of these work: Claude Code (on 0G Private Computer or an Anthropic plan ), Codex , Gemini CLI or Antigravity CLI .
Cloning matters: the assistant reuses this repo's tools/disable.sh and launcher/build-and-install.sh instead of writing its own, and that is where the backup, the Home guard and the restore record live.
The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks each step with screenshots pulled from the TV. With this repo as context it takes about fifteen minutes.
A home screen that looks like an Apple TV and gets out of the way:
And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics phoning home, no apps you never asked for.
Anything running Android TV or Google TV .
Tested lists from contributors, one folder per model in examples/ . The brands with the most lists, each linked to its models on the website:

Find your TV: search cleanyour.tv/tvs or the full table in examples/README.md .
Your TV not here? The prompt discovers the bloat itself. Add your list afterwards and the next person with your model skips that step: CONTRIBUTING.md .
Everything the assistant does, you can run yourself. Two things have to be on the computer first:
tools/tv.py talks to network ADB on port 5555. If that port stays closed and the TV offers Wireless debugging with a pairing code (the Chromecast with Google TV and the Google TV Streamer do), pair it once with the stock adb and run adb tcpip 5555 first, as Troubleshooting describes.
The scripts never leave the TV without a Home app: they only disable a stock launcher they recognise, and skip the Home app in a list until another launcher answers HOME. Your own lists can live outside the repository: list paths are relative to the directory you run from, and absolute paths work too.
Every script has a PowerShell twin next to it. Install Python 3 and a JDK from 17 through 22, and in the SDK Manager add platform 34 and build-tools 34 (34.0.0 or any newer 34.x). The script uses JAVA_HOME when it points at a JDK in that range, and otherwise Android Studio's bundled JDK when that JDK is in the same range:
The last two are the undo and a theme push, the tools/restore.sh and tools/theme.sh lines the sections above give in bash. On Google TV the undo takes the stock launcher as well: -Stock com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx .
The install scripts ask the TV which launcher owns Home and only disable one they recognise, the four in KNOWN_STOCK_LAUNCHERS : com.google.android.tvlauncher , com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx , com.google.android.leanbacklauncher and Xiaomi's com.mitv.tvhome (PatchWall). Pass STOCK_LAUNCHER= ( -StockLauncher ) to override, or none to leave it alone.
tools/disable.sh ( disable.ps1 ) applies the same rule before it disables anything:
If the list contains the app that owns Home and no other app on the TV answers HOME, it skips that entry, says why, and disables the rest of the list. So a list applied before the launcher handover cannot leave the TV with nothing to start.
The setup wizard, the settings apps, a vendor FallbackHome and factory-test apps (Xiaomi's com.duokan.factorytest ) answer HOME too and don't count.
On Google TV it also keeps the owner while setupwraith answers HOME and stays enabled (not listed, or kept for the Wi-Fi network): setupwraith answers ahead of an installed launcher that is not Home yet, so it would take Home.
Run the same list again once launcher/build-and-install.sh has made the new launcher Home and the entry is applied; FORCE_HOME=1 ( $env:FORCE_HOME ) disables it anyway.
The microphone, and what can be said about it
"Which of these packages is listening?" has no honest one-line answer: a permission scan shows fifty system packages with RECORD_AUDIO that record nothing, and ACR clients see the screen with no audio permission at all. tools/privacy.py reports what the TV actually says, with the evidence for each voice, ACR and telemetry candidate: TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/privacy.py , and --write turns them into a normal debloat list. What the audit cannot do is prove intent: docs/privacy.md explains why.
A small native home screen for Android TV: about 572 KB , plain Java, built for TVs with 1 GB of RAM. No blur, no video, no network permission, no background services. The TV needs Android 8.0 (API 26) or newer, the minSdk in launcher/app/build.gradle ; what is left on an older set is in Troubleshooting .
Themes, switches and add-ons together, with screenshots: cleanyour.tv/addons .
More: docs/launcher.md has the launcher settings page row by row, changing the default home, the languages, remote keys, the Clock screensaver, navigation and building it yourself.
Keep the list you applied. One line puts the TV back the way it was:
More: docs/restore.md has what the record holds, when the stock launcher argument counts, and what happens without a record.
An update installs over the cleaned-up system: the listed packages come back, Home goes to the stock launcher, and new preloads appear that no list mentions. Open ADB again as in Quick start step 1, then compare the TV with the list you applied; --fix puts it back:
More: docs/firmware-updates.md has the exit codes, a weekly check, what --fix changes, TVs that keep the stock launcher as Home, and lists that disable the updater.
The full list of things that bit us is in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md . The three that matter most:
🍎 macOS blocks adb connect ("No route to host") under Local Network privacy. tools/tv.py avoids the binary.
⚠️ Disable the stock launcher only after the new one is installed and running , or Home lands on a factory test app. The install script orders this for you.
🔁 On Google TV the setup wizard ( com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith ) can take Home and crash-loop the system after the stock launcher is disabled. Disable it too, and list it in your debloat.txt so restore brings it back. But check dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*' first: if the Wi-Fi network was saved during setup it belongs to setupwraith, and disabling it deletes the network (re-join it in Settings first; tools/disable.sh skips setupwraith until you do). On Google's own Chromecast and on the Google TV Streamer it also costs phone casting, see Troubleshooting . Stuck already? tools/tv.py 'pm enable --user 0 com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx' .

Yes. Independent developers have built free, open-source apps on CleanYourTV's TV lists that do the cleanup over Wi-Fi, with no coding agent. Each shows a plan first, only switches apps off, and can put everything back:
These apps are independent projects, not affiliated with or endorsed by CleanYourTV or its maintainer, and each is provided as is under its own license. Report app problems in that app's repo. More at cleanyour.tv/app .
Nothing is flashed, rooted or deleted; packages are disabled in the user profile. The risk is disabling something the TV leans on, which is why lists are applied in small batches with a restore script ready. The TV's own Settings → Apps page can re-enable packages even without the tools. If the TV no longer starts far enough for that, a factory reset from its recovery menu is usually the way back.
The updater is left on in most lists, so firmware updates arrive as usual. Some lists disable the TV's own updater, and on those a firmware update arrives only when you re-enable it. When one does land it installs over the cleaned-up system, so a package comes back and you re-run the script: see After a firmware update .
Streaming apps still update through the Play Store, which is left alone. The launcher just lists what is installed and launches it with intents that have been stable for a decade.
Hold OK on Settings (top right) and choose Reorder apps . OK picks an app up, the arrows move it, Back places it, and Back again finishes. Holding OK on a tile also offers Move ( tile_menu , on by default), which picks that app up straight away. More: docs/launcher.md
Yes, over a private Tailscale link instead of the same Wi-Fi: either Tailscale on their TV, shared with you, or a computer or Apple TV at their home routing to it. Never by opening the ADB port on their router. Step by step in docs/REMOTE.md .
It is one explicit "allow this computer" tap on the TV, the same as developing an Android app. Network ADB is plaintext on port 5555, and on some firmware any device on the LAN gets a shell, so close it when you are done:
On the TV: Developer options → turn USB debugging , Network/ADB debugging and Wireless debugging off, whichever the TV has, and revoke the USB debugging authorisations.
Reboot the TV, then confirm the port is gone from your computer: python3 tools/adb-closed.py must say the port is closed.
The launcher keeps working without debugging. More, including checking Wireless debugging's own port: docs/faq.md
Partly, with Android's Private DNS (Android 9 and newer). Point it at an ad-blocking resolver such as AdGuard DNS and every app's ad and tracker domains stop resolving, system-wide, surviving reboots. The trade-off: that resolver then sees every DNS query the TV makes, and it does not remove YouTube ads.
More, with the two commands and how to switch back: docs/faq.md
A few, and they need no ADB: the advertising ID, Location, Usage & diagnostics and Scanning always available, plus Apps only mode where the stock launcher stays. Flip Usage & diagnostics before the debloat; on some TVs its page goes with it.
More, with the paths for Google TV, Android TV and Fire OS: docs/faq.md
Not from this repo. Chromecast built-in stays for Android phones. For iPhones, jqssun/android-airplay-server works; an install script for it is in PR #84 .
Build it with the one-line script in Doing it by hand ; it takes a minute and you control what goes on your TV. That needs the JDK and Android SDK named there. No prebuilt binaries.
On 17 October 2026 I posted a before and after of my parents' TV, cleaned up by Claude Code over Wi-Fi. It reached 8.6M views, people started doing the same to their own TVs, and their replies turned into the lists here: 170+ TV models from 200+ contributors in the first four days. The repo was called tv-vibehack until the 19th; old links work.
Two weeks on, it was the #1 trending repository on GitHub for the week of 19–25 October, with over 46K stars and 5.7K forks, and 1.4M views and 260K clones in 14 days. The lists now cover 407 TV models from 106 brands. The coverage: 412 articles from 54 countries and 229 videos on YouTube and Bilibili, all in docs/PRESS.md (numbers as of 30 October 2026).
The most useful contribution is your TV's debloat list, so the next person with that model does not have to rediscover it. CONTRIBUTING.md has the format and the testing we ask for. Contributing through a coding agent? AGENTS.md gives it the same rules.
CleanYourTV is an independent open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by any TV maker or platform. Brand and model names are used only to say which TV a list was tested on, and remain the trademarks of their owners.
It works only through settings the TV itself offers to its owner: Developer options, ADB debugging and Android's own pm disable-user , the same switch as Settings > Apps > Disable. It does not root the TV, flash firmware, or bypass any lock, DRM or copy protection, and the repo contains no manufacturer software, firmware or APKs.
Nothing is uninstalled, and tools/restore.sh puts everything back. You run it on a TV you own, at your own risk, and changing a TV's software may affect its warranty or support.
